title: Table
summary: A data table. Two modes: hand it a raw table in the default slot (rows and cells exactly as authored) and it supplies the scroll frame, toolbar, bulk, empty and footer slots; or give it columns and rows and it renders the table itself, with sorting, filtering, selection, loading and phone cards. The data-driven mode: striped, hover, bordered, density, sticky header and first column, sortable headers, filter row, row selection with a bulk bar, loading and empty states, expandable detail rows and a card layout on a phone. Custom cell content goes in slots named cell-<rowId>-<key>; expandable rows show the slot detail-<rowId>. With manual set, the host owns sorting, filtering and paging and the element only renders and reports. At 500 rows or more (a fixed threshold; js/table-vw.js), a non-expandable, non-slotted table windows: only the rows near the scroll frame's viewport are drawn, and sort, filter and selection still act on every row. In data-driven mode, each row carries data-pk-context="<rowId>", so wrapping the whole table in a pk-context-menu can serve different menu content per row (see that element's context field); js/context-actions.js's wireContextMenu(menuEl, { items, run }) is the shared plumbing for that: it paints the { action, label, shortcut?, disabled?, danger? } list a row's own state calls for and dispatches a choice through the same run(action) an existing toolbar or keyboard shortcut already uses (issue #586). With editable set, cells of columns with an editor edit in place (pk-cell-edit, cellErrors); an editable table windows too (#1474): the active row and the row being edited stay drawn wherever they are, arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown and Ctrl+Home/End move by row id, and paste and undo reach rows that are not drawn. Rows must keep a fixed height, so an expandable table never windows (host-slotted cells stay in the light DOM; the card layout on a phone is not measured).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions: { key, label, type?: text|number|date, align?: start|end, sortable?, hidePhone?, shed?: 1|2|3, title?, editor?: text|number|select|date|textarea|combobox, options?, free?, required?, min?, max?, maxLength? }[]. A JSON attribute or a property. type decides how the column sorts and filters, not how a value is shown: cells always show the row value as given, as text, and the element does no formatting, locale or time zone handling, so the host sends the display string it wants ("$1,204.50", "7 Jan 2026"). number sorts numerically and reads through currency symbols and grouping ("$1,204.50" is 1204.5; text that holds no number sorts first) and aligns to the end unless align says otherwise. date sorts chronologically by Date.parse of the value, so use ISO 8601 (a date-only value such as 2026-01-07 is read as UTC midnight, a value with an offset keeps it; text that does not parse sorts first). text sorts alphabetically with numeric collation, ignoring case. In an editable table a column with an editor is editable: editor is text, number, select (with options: strings or { value, label }) textarea (Enter commits, Shift+Enter adds a line), combobox (a native input with a list of options; the text must be an option's value or label unless free; pk-cell-query lets the host fill the list as the user types) or date (a native date input; the cell value is an ISO 8601 date such as 2026-01-07, and min and max are ISO dates, checked as "On or after" and "On or before"), and required, min, max and maxLength are checked before a value is committed. hidePhone hides the column below 640px, in the cards layout too. shed drops the column by the table's own width, wherever the table sits: 3 below 48rem, 2 below 36rem, 1 below 24rem, so the higher number goes first and one table sheds its derived columns in a narrow pane or card before it scrolls sideways; the cards layout keeps every column. title marks the column that names the row (put it first): in the phone cards layout its cell is the card heading, with no label, the full width, start-aligned, wrapped and in heading weight, and its data-label is omitted; on a wide screen it is an ordinary cell. A label of "" also omits data-label, so no label is drawn in a card.

props.name: rows
props.description: Row data, one object per row. A JSON attribute or a property. Custom cell content goes in the cell-<rowId>-<key> slots, expanded content in detail-<rowId>. Two optional row fields mark a row: tone (warning, positive, accent or critical) tints it and draws a leading rule, and indent (1 or 2) steps it in, for rows that need attention or sit under a parent; both carry through to the phone card (issue 1019). Any other value is ignored.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: The field that identifies a row.

props.name: striped
props.description: Alternate row tint.

props.name: hover
props.description: Tint the row under the pointer.

props.name: bordered
props.description: Border on every cell.

props.name: density
props.description: Cell padding step.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: Pin the header row (give the table a maxHeight).

props.name: stickyColumn
props.description: Pin the first column.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Checkbox column with select-all.

props.name: clickable
props.description: Rows are activatable: they show a pointer, take the keyboard (each row is a tab stop; Enter or Space on the row) and fire pk-row-click.

props.name: rowHrefTemplate
props.description: Row links: /orders/{id} or #/orders/{id} ({field} too, URL-encoded). The first cell links; a click goes through the router.

props.name: navigate
props.description: Who follows a row link: router (default, empty), host or none.

props.name: currentRow
props.description: The id of the row that is open elsewhere (the record shown in a detail pane): that row is tinted, marked with an accent bar and given aria-current. The host sets it (from the route, or from pk-row-click); the element never changes it. Empty marks no row.

props.name: filterable
props.description: A filter input under each header.

props.name: manual
props.description: The host sorts, filters and pages; rows are shown exactly as given.

props.name: sort
props.description: Key of the column being sorted; empty when the rows are in their natural order.

props.name: sortDir
props.description: Sort direction.

props.name: filters
props.description: Filter text per column key: { [key]: text }.

props.name: selected
props.description: Ids of the selected rows. The user changes it with the row checkboxes and the element raises pk-select with the new ids; a change the host makes raises nothing. In a manual table the ids of rows that are not loaded stay (paging, searching and sorting replace the rows, not the selection); see total and selectScope for selecting every row of the query.

props.name: total
props.description: How many rows match the current query across all pages (a manual table shows one page of them). With a total larger than the loaded rows, once every loaded row is selected the bulk bar offers a "Select all N rows" button, which raises pk-select-all with scope "all". 0 means unknown or not paged: no button. The selection survives the host replacing the rows (paging, search, sort): ids are kept, not matched against the loaded rows, so clear selected when the query changes if the selection should not outlive it.

props.name: selectPageOnly
props.description: Never offer "Select all N rows" (it needs total): the header checkbox selects the loaded page and the scope stays "page". For a list whose bulk action works only on explicit ids.

props.name: selectScope
props.description: "all" after the user chose "Select all N rows": every row of the query counts as selected, though selected holds only the ids that were loaded. Any change of the selection, and a host that empties selected, sets it back to "page". The element sets it; a host may set it to restore a state.

props.name: editable
props.description: Inline cell editing: the table becomes an ARIA grid with one active cell (arrow keys, Home, End move it; Tab moves it right along the row, then leaves the grid at the row's last cell rather than trapping focus), and a cell of a column that has an editor opens with Enter, F2, a second click or tap on the active cell, or by typing a printable character (which replaces the cell's content, as in a spreadsheet). While editing, Enter commits the draft and moves the active cell down one row, Tab commits and moves it right, Escape cancels, and leaving the cell commits. A cell the host fills through a cell-<rowId>-<key> slot is read-only to the table and owned by the host (a pk-switch there toggles itself): give the control tabindex="-1" so the cell stays the one tab stop, and an accessible name; Space or Enter on the cell moves focus to the control, and Escape in the control returns focus to the cell. Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes the last committed edit of this table (up to 100) and Ctrl+Y or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z redoes it; each step goes through pk-cell-edit, so the host may refuse it. Pasting tab-separated text (copied from a spreadsheet) with a cell active fills a block from that cell: each cell is checked and offered through pk-cell-edit (source paste), read-only columns and cells beyond the grid are skipped, invalid cells show aria-invalid and the rest commit, one undo takes the whole paste back, and pk-cells-paste summarises it. Shift+arrows, Shift+PageUp/PageDown, Shift+Ctrl+Home/End and Shift+click extend a rectangular selection (aria-selected on each selected cell, aria-multiselectable on the grid) by row id, so it spans rows that are not drawn; a plain move or Escape collapses it. Ctrl/Cmd+D fills the top row of the selection down its rows, each cell through pk-cell-edit (source fill), read-only columns and refused values skipped, one undo for the whole fill; Ctrl/Cmd+C copies the selection (or the active cell) as tab-separated text. A commit raises pk-cell-edit, and unless the host cancels it the row holds the new value. A host that saves asynchronously calls event.detail.wait(promise) in its pk-cell-edit handler: the value shows at once and the cell is aria-busy (dimmed) until the promise settles; if it rejects, the previous value comes back without a new event, the cell shows the rejection's message (or "Not saved") with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, the edit leaves the undo history and a polite status says so (a fulfilment announces "saved"); the answers of a paste or fill are handled together. A message on a cell that is not being edited (a refused paste, a failed save) is shown below the cell while it is hovered or focused and is always read by assistive technology; it never wraps inside a narrow column. At 500 rows or more it windows like a read-only table (see the summary): the active row and the row being edited stay drawn.

props.name: cellErrors
props.description: Cells the host marks invalid: { "<rowId>:<key>": "message" }. The cell shows the message and aria-invalid. Set it in a pk-cell-edit handler that cancels the event (the editor stays open on the message), or after a server check. The element never changes it.

props.name: expandable
props.description: Rows that have a detail-<rowId> slot get a toggle that shows or hides that slot under the row.

props.name: expander
props.description: Set to none to leave out the toggle column of an expandable table: the host opens rows from its own control (a disclosure inside a cell) by setting expanded, which is still honoured, and the detail-<rowId> slots are still shown for the ids in it.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Ids of the expanded rows. The user changes it and pk-row-expand reports each change; after that the host owns it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a placeholder row, announce Loading and mark the table busy.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Text shown when there are no rows. The empty slot replaces it.

props.name: cards
props.description: Each row becomes a card below 640px.

props.name: caption
props.description: Table caption.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrolling region.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Bounds the frame; sticky header and column need it.

props.name: flow
props.description: Slotted-table mode: no scroll frame, for a table inside a container that already scrolls.

slots.description: A raw table (thead, tbody, tfoot, any rows). The page-level layer styles it; the element frames it.

slots.name: toolbar
slots.description: Search, filters and buttons above the table, laid out in a wrapping row. Give the item that should sit at the far end (an action button beside a search box) the attribute data-end: it and the items after it move to the end of the row. pk-table-filters (issue 203) fits here: a debounced search box plus a Filters trigger and panel around your own filter fields, so a table gets consistent search/filter UI without a page rebuilding that shell by hand.

slots.name: bulk
slots.description: Actions shown while rows are selected.

slots.name: cell-<rowId>-<key>
slots.description: Custom content for one cell of a data-driven table: rowId is the row's rowKey value, key the column key. Replaces the cell text. In an editable table the cell is read-only to the table; a control in it (a pk-switch) is the host's: tabindex="-1" on it keeps the cell the one tab stop, and its own change event carries the value.

slots.name: header-<key>
slots.description: Content beside the title of one column header of a data-driven table (key is the column key): a help tooltip, an icon button, a menu. The text title (and the sort button) stays; the slotted content sits after it, outside the sort button, so using it never sorts, and it is a tab stop of its own. Give an action control an accessible name. Hidden with the header row in the phone card layout.

slots.name: detail-<rowId>
slots.description: Detail content of one row, shown under it when the row is expanded (expandable). A row without this slot has no toggle.

slots.name: detail-<rowId>.<name>
slots.description: A further detail panel of one row, shown under it when expanded holds the string "<rowId>.<name>". A row can have several, plus detail-<rowId>. Named panels have no built-in toggle: the host opens them by setting expanded (use expander="none" to drop the toggle column altogether).

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Empty state; an pk-empty-state fits. Replaces emptyText.

slots.name: footer
slots.description: Below the table; an pk-pagination fits.

slots.name: foot
slots.description: Data-driven mode: a footer or summary row (totals, a note that the figures do not add up). One tfoot cell spanning every column after the rows on a desktop; a full-width trailing card after the last card on a phone. Raw mode authors its own tfoot instead.

events.name: pk-sort
events.description: A sortable header was activated. Each activation of the same header cycles ascending, descending, then cleared: a cleared sort reports key and direction null and the rows return to their natural order (a manual table reports it too, and the host restores its own order). Cancel to keep the current sort.

events.name: pk-navigate
events.description: A plain click on a row link (see rowHrefTemplate); cancel it to navigate yourself, else the browser follows the link.

events.name: pk-row-click
events.description: A clickable row was activated by a click, or by Enter or Space while the row itself has focus. A click or key on a checkbox, button, link or select inside the row does not raise it.

events.name: pk-select-all
events.description: Raised on a table that has a total (the rows are paged by the host) when the user selects every loaded row (scope "page", count the rows on the page; pk-select carries the ids as well) or chooses "Select all N" (scope "all", count the total; no ids: the host expands the scope by asking its data source again, with the query it has). selectScope is then "all" until the selection changes.

events.name: pk-row-expand
events.description: The user expanded or collapsed a row. expanded is the new state; the expanded prop already holds it.

events.name: pk-cell-edit
events.description: An edited cell is about to be committed (an editable table). value is typed by the column (a number for a number editor, else text) and previous is the value it replaces; the event only fires when they differ, after the element checked required, min, max and maxLength. Cancel it to reject the value: the editor stays open showing cellErrors for the cell, or "Value not accepted". source says where it came from: keyboard, paste, fill, undo or redo (undo and redo carry the value being restored); a paste raises it once per cell. Not cancelled, the table replaces its rows with a copy that holds the value and the host takes it from there. detail.wait(promise) (a function, not serialised) tells the table the host is still saving: see the editable field.

events.name: pk-cell-query
events.description: The user typed in a combobox cell editor. Call detail.set(options) (strings or { value, label }) with the suggestions to show; use free on the column to accept values outside them.

events.name: pk-cells-paste
events.description: A paste into an editable table finished. cells lists the cells that took a value ({ id, key, value }); rejected lists those that did not ({ row, col, reason }: outside the grid, readonly, a failed check message, or refused by a cancelled pk-cell-edit). Each accepted cell already raised pk-cell-edit with source paste.

parts.name: bulk-all
parts.description: The button that widens the selection to every row of the query ("Select all 112 rows"), then clears it ("Clear selection"). Shown only with a total.

parts.name: foot
parts.description: The single cell of the foot row (in a tfoot), spanning every column.

cssProperties.name: --pk-table-max-height
cssProperties.description: Height of the scrolling frame (set from maxHeight).

methods.name: sortBy(key, direction)
methods.description: Sort programmatically. sortBy(null) clears the sort.

a11y: A real table with a caption, aria-rowcount and aria-busy. Sortable headers hold a button and carry aria-sort. The scrolling frame is a labelled focusable region so the keyboard can scroll it. A clickable row is focusable (one tab stop per row, before the checkbox and buttons inside it) and Enter or Space on it activates it, with a visible focus ring; the controls inside a row keep their own keys. Each expandable row has a real button (Enter or Space) with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at its detail row, and keeps focus after it toggles. The loading row carries a status text. Checkboxes name their row; the selection count is a polite status, and the "Select all N rows" / "Clear selection" button inside it is a real button (a tab stop, named with the count) whose change of text is announced by the same status. The card layout keeps the header for assistive technology. Cell values are set as text, never parsed as HTML. The current row (current-row) carries aria-current="true", so a screen reader announces which record is open. An editable table is role="grid": one cell is the tab stop (arrow keys, Home and End move it, Tab moves and commits), the active cell has aria-selected, a cell that cannot be edited has aria-readonly, a cell whose save the host has not answered yet has aria-busy, an invalid cell has aria-invalid and its message is tied to its editor with aria-describedby, every editor is named ", row " (a control the host slots into a cell needs its own name: the pk-switch's own text, e.g. Listed, row 1 to keep it off the screen), and a committed or cancelled edit is announced in a polite status region. When the rows are windowed (500 or more) aria-rowcount is the whole view plus the header and every drawn row carries its aria-rowindex; PageUp, PageDown, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End move by rows and announce "Row N of M".
